title: Supreme Court registry explains the new steps for filing urgent mentioning requests
excerpt: A short explainer on how advocates can now submit urgent mentioning requests online, and what details the registry asks for before listing.

title: Allahabad High Court publishes an updated calendar for the coming term
excerpt: The calendar lists working days, vacation benches and the dates on which fresh matters will be taken up at the principal seat and the Lucknow Bench.

title: Delhi High Court opens a help desk for first-time e-filers
excerpt: Litigants filing without an advocate can get step-by-step help with scanning, page limits and fee payment at the new desk.

title: What a draft bill’s public consultation period means, and how to send comments
excerpt: A plain-language guide to the consultation process for draft legislation: where drafts are published, the usual time window, and how comments are submitted.

title: Supreme Court bench to take up a batch of tenancy appeals after the break
excerpt: Several connected appeals on rent and eviction disputes have been tagged together and are expected to be listed once the court reopens.

title: Lucknow Bench issues a notice on the format for case-status enquiries
excerpt: Parties are asked to quote the case number and year in a fixed format so enquiries can be answered faster at the counter and online.

title: Delhi district courts extend evening sittings for traffic challan matters
excerpt: The extended hours are meant to reduce waiting time for people settling challans in person, according to the notice.

title: Explainer: how a bill becomes law, from introduction to notification
excerpt: Readings, committee review, assent and notification: a step-by-step walk-through of the legislative process with the terms you are likely to see in the news.

title: Supreme Court e-committee shares tips for joining hearings by video
excerpt: The note covers device checks, naming your video window with the item number, and what to do if the connection drops during a hearing.

title: Allahabad High Court mediation centre announces weekend sessions
excerpt: Parties referred to mediation can now choose weekend slots, which the centre says should help working litigants attend.

title: Delhi High Court legal services committee schedules free legal-aid camps
excerpt: Camps will be held across several court complexes, with volunteers explaining eligibility for free legal aid and how to apply.

title: Rules notified under a state act: where to read them and what changes
excerpt: When rules are notified under an act, they set out the procedure. This piece explains where notified rules are published and how to read them.

title: Supreme Court publishes a guide to reading its daily cause list
excerpt: Item numbers, court numbers, and the difference between fresh and after-notice matters, explained with a sample page.

title: Prayagraj district court moves copying section requests online
excerpt: Certified-copy applications can now be filed and tracked online, with collection slots offered at the counter.

title: Saket court complex adds a facilitation centre for senior citizens
excerpt: The centre offers seating, help with forms and a separate queue for senior citizens attending hearings.

title: Consumer protection basics: where to file, and the role of each commission
excerpt: District, state and national commissions hear consumer complaints. This explainer covers how the forum is chosen and what a complaint usually includes.

title: Supreme Court library opens its reading room to registered interns
excerpt: Interns attached to advocates-on-record can apply for reading-room passes, subject to the library’s timings and rules.

title: Kanpur Nagar district court sets up a token system at the filing counter
excerpt: Tokens are issued on arrival and displayed on screens, replacing the earlier single queue at the main counter.

title: Delhi High Court reminds litigants to update phone numbers for SMS alerts
excerpt: Listing and order alerts are sent by SMS, so parties are asked to keep their registered mobile numbers current with the registry.

title: What “commencement” means: why an act can be passed but not yet in force
excerpt: An act can come into force on a date set by notification, sometimes section by section. Here is how to check which parts are in force.

title: Supreme Court shares updated guidance on paper-book page limits
excerpt: The guidance sets out font, margin and page-numbering requirements for paper books filed in fresh matters.

title: Varanasi district court launches a kiosk for case-status look-ups
excerpt: Visitors can search by case number or party name at the kiosk near the main gate, in Hindi or English.

title: Rohini courts publish a map of courtrooms and help desks
excerpt: The printable map marks courtrooms, the record room, the legal-aid desk and accessible entrances in the complex.

title: Ordinances explained: when they are issued and how long they last
excerpt: An ordinance has the force of law for a limited time unless it is replaced by an act. This explainer covers the basics in plain words.

title: Supreme Court’s legal services committee lists its free-help channels
excerpt: A round-up of the helpline, walk-in desk and online form for people who want to know whether they qualify for free legal aid.

title: Agra and Ghaziabad district courts align e-payment options for court fees
excerpt: Both courts now accept the same set of online payment methods for court fees, according to their notices.

title: Dwarka courts introduce SMS reminders a day before hearings
excerpt: Parties with registered mobile numbers will get a reminder with the courtroom and item number the evening before.

title: Reading a gazette notification: the parts that matter
excerpt: Number, date, the enabling section and the operative text: how to read a gazette notification without getting lost.

title: Gautam Buddh Nagar district court adds a second e-seva kendra
excerpt: The new centre helps litigants and advocates with e-filing, case status and certified copies during court hours.

title: Karkardooma courts move lost-and-found to the facilitation centre
excerpt: Items found in the complex will now be logged and held at the facilitation centre near the main entrance.
